item.title: Old post, but
item.content:encoded:
While it's true the Foundation will always place the continued survival of humanity above all else, it seems like it'd be conductive to this goal to treat sapient skips well. It means they'll be less complaints about the foundation staff abusing anomalies for no good reason, avoiding possible budget cuts and making it harder to capture entities down the line. In addition to that, if the SCP feels "at home" it's more likely to comply with the Foundation

The Foundation staff is full of people who willingly sent prisoners to die agonizing deaths, they can probably call somebody by their name without compromising their ability to act cold and rational.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
What MMG said. This is just your headcanon. I get equally frustrated when I see the opposite (abusive Foundation) because it's not what I like, just like this isn't what you like. And honestly, it's not just that I don't like it, it's that it doesn't make sense to me, for all the reasons MMG said and all the reasons I had the Committee give in this article.

So do you think that in psychiatric hospitals and rehab programs IRL, patients get called a number and experiemented on without their consent? No? That would be nuts because ~it's real life~, right? Well, could it be because the people holding them know they're not criminals and deserve to be treated with at least a little respect, because they don't even want to be there and don't objectively 'deserve' it?

Well, there you have it. SCPs are not inmates, they are closer to patients. The Foundation's job is "secure, contain, protect" and all of those things are possible even with a demeanor that isn't shitty. "Research" has never been a priority in the Foundation's mission, you know.

I'm starting to dislike this whole push for a progressive, diverse Foundation.

…Then again, if you're a user who thinks basic respectful treatment is political and especially ~progressive~, we may not get anywhere.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
This is neither how scientists or security officers operate in real life. Scientists regularly humanise the objects of their study (see: any biologist, ever) and there are reasons why both modern hospitals and prisons (combined, a reasonable approximation for what the Foundation is) advise staff to refer to their charges by their names instead of Prisoner #10485 or whatever; it improves their behaviour and cooperation for zero cost. If you object to this you are objecting based on ideology, not practicality.

(Security/prison guards do ignore people's pronouns and names and refer to them by dehumanising designations, but this is not an efficient way to run a system - it is purely done for various security theater political purposes)

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
This is well done, and I normally like this sort of writing, but it was even a little too dry for my taste. Novote.

I don't think the III/IV qualifying parameters make a whole lot of sense - neither are mutually exclusive of one another on a scale which should be stepped gradients of risk. The fact that someone was originally non-anomalous and contacted the Foundation has no relevance to whether they should be allowed to wear plainclothes or own gifted items, if someone who is compliant and cooperative is forbidden from doing so (why?). Maybe this could be a privilege incentive structure to encourage people to turn themselves in, but not if the criteria are closed to the public.

There may be intentional inconsistencies to demonstrate how the Foundation is still an arbitrary and repressive organisation, but it's not clear, and I don't really like that sort of device.

item.title: Author Post
item.content:encoded:
Coldpost. Potentially a bad idea because this is potentially boring as shit. But I had a lot of Feelings to get out.

Edit to elaborate:

For in-universe reasons I thought this should exist: Read what the Committee has to say. For out-of-universe reasons I thought this should exist: 1) I'm exhausted by the evil portrayal of the Foundation; 'organization that dehumanizes weird people and takes them away' has been done to death in sci-fi and primarily superhero fiction, and there's nothing interesting to come from the relationship between the parties if all that happens between them is textbook mistreatment
